title: finding(ci): objectui's half-state patrol RUNS but its findings reach nobody — the run summary is unreadable from a seat, and the one exit code that is readable does not mean "clean"
body:
The half-state sweep **runs on this repo four times a day and completes**, but its findings are delivered ONLY to the workflow run summary — and the run summary is **not reachable from an agent seat's API surface**. So every execution seat's first judgement of every fire is a leg it cannot read.

⛔ This is ⛔ not a bug report against `half-state-patrol.yml`: running without an anchor is an **explicitly supported** configuration here (objectui#8740), and the workflow says so in its own notice. This card is about the consequence for this repo specifically, and it has a one-action remedy the workflow itself documents.

## Measured, 2026-09-18T09:07Z

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| `half-state-patrol.yml` runs on objectstack-ai/objectui | **108** total; latest run `35320759072`, created 2026-09-18T07:42:55Z, conclusion **success** |
| the sweep itself | job log line, verbatim: `check-half-states exited 0` at 2026-09-18T07:45:01Z, with `PM_SWEEP_REPO: objectstack-ai/objectui` and `PM_SWEEP_CLOSED_FLOOR: 2026-08-28` |
| `ANCHOR_ISSUE` in that run's env | **empty** — printed as `ANCHOR_ISSUE: ` in three separate step groups |
| the notice the run emitted | «No anchor issue configured for objectstack-ai/objectui, which is a supported configuration here (objectui#8740). The sweep RAN and its rendered body is in this run's summary…» |
| the rendered body, via the check-runs API | `output.summary` length **0**, `output.text` length **0** |

⇒ the sweep is **alive**, and what it found is **unreadable** from here. The rendered report exists only in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which the API does not return for an Actions job.

## ⚠️ And the one number that IS readable does not mean what it looks like

`check-half-states exited 0` is reachable through the job log. ⛔ **It does not mean the board is clean.** `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`'s own header says so, at its line 65 and line 80:

> ## Why report-only, and why the exit code is ALWAYS 0 on a completed sweep
> … a completed sweep exits 0 **whether it found 0 or 40 violations**

⇒ the exit code discriminates **completed versus did-not-run**, and nothing more. (Exit 2 = usage error; exit 3 = prerequisite not met.)

⚠️ Filed with the near-miss attached, because it is the point of the card: the filing seat read `exited 0` and formed the belief «no half-states on the board» **before** reading that header. The header is what stopped it. A number that is reachable while the thing it seems to report is not is exactly the shape that produces a confident wrong reading.

## What the invisibility has cost, measured on this board today

This seat found **three** half-states **by hand** during one shift, none of them via the patrol:

- **objectui#9061** — `pm:dispatched` with **no assignee** since 2026-09-13, five days, because PR objectui#9138 merged with no `Fixes` line. It was in that state when the 07:45Z sweep ran, and ⛔ there is no way from here to tell whether the sweep flagged it.
- **objectui#9782** and **objectui#9710** — both auto-closed `completed` while still carrying `pm:dispatched` **and** an assignee (the `Fixes` auto-close never strips either). Both were cleaned by hand within minutes, but only because a seat happened to be watching the merge.

## The remedy, quoted from the workflow rather than invented

`.github/workflows/half-state-patrol.yml:257-261`:

> TO ADOPT (a sibling repo): change NOTHING here — set the repository variable, or set nothing and read the run summaries (objectui#8740).

and `:263-265`:

> The anchor deliberately carries `tracking` and NO `domain:*` label: `tracking` is in the sweeper's own `H13_EXEMPT_LABELS`, so the anchor can never appear as a finding in the sweep it hosts.

Two steps: open a `tracking`-labelled issue in this repo carrying **no** `domain:*` label, then set the repository variable `HALF_STATE_ANCHOR_ISSUE` to its number (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables).

⚠️ **Step 2 is a maintainer action.** A repository variable is outside an agent seat's API surface, so ⛔ no seat can do it and ⛔ no seat should be asked to. Step 1 a seat can do, but ⛔ doing it alone would leave a `tracking` issue nothing points at — a new half-state — so both belong in one act.

⚠️ Checked before proposing: this repo has **8** open `tracking` issues and ⛔ none is a patrol anchor (six carry a `domain:*` label, which the workflow's own text disqualifies). Control, same query shape, same run: `pm:seat` returns 5 rows, so the 8 is a positive result.

## What would make this not worth doing

If the maintainer's intent is that objectui's half-states are healed by seats noticing them at the moment of landing — which is what happened to two of the three above — then the accepted trade the workflow already names («it notifies nobody, by accepted trade») stands and this card closes. ⇒ the call is whose eyes the findings are for, ⛔ not whether the sweep works.

## Dedupe words

- half-state patrol anchor objectui unset
- `HALF_STATE_ANCHOR_ISSUE` repository variable
- run summary not reachable from API
- `check-half-states exited 0` does not mean clean
- patrol findings notify nobody

## Related

objectui#8740 (the card that made the no-anchor configuration supported) · objectui#9061 / objectui#9782 / objectui#9710 (the three half-states found by hand today)
